title: Comparative Morpho-anatomy and Histochemistry of Six Brazilian Rainforest Native Species: Aiouea spp. (Lauraceae)
content:
Abstract
Lauraceae Juss. is distributed worldwide and is well known for the difficulty in the identification of its species. The genus Aiouea, native to Brazil, is part of this family and has gained attention for the biological potential of its species. Apart from that, there are no data in the literature on the morpho-anatomical study of the Aiouea genus to aid in the correct identification and differentiation of its species. Therefore, the aim of this study was to provide detailed morpho-anatomical characteristics of leaves and stems of Aiouea acarodomatifera Kosterm., Aiouea amoena (Nees & Mart.) R.Rohde, Aiouea glaziovii (Mez) R.Rohde, Aiouea montana (Sw.) R.Rohde, Aiouea sellowiana (Nees & Mart.) R.Rohde, and Aiouea stenophylla (Meisn.) R.Rohde, using light and scanning electron microscopy techniques, as well as histochemical tests. The leaves and stems of the six species analyzed, although sharing basic anatomical features, present characteristics that, when analyzed as a group, form a fingerprint for each species. The notable diagnostic features include the presence or absence of non-glandular trichomes, papillose epidermis, and sclereids, as well as the occurrence and morphotypes of calcium oxalate crystals.
